```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(MixSIARPFN)
ok <- MixSIARPFN:::networks_ready()   # the code needs the networks (see pfn_networks())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ok,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
num <- function(x, digits = 2) if (ok) format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits) else "?"
```

This follows MixSIAR's mantis shrimp example script (`mixsiar_script_mantis.R`): mantis
shrimp from several habitats, two tracers (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N) and six prey sources. It
uses three options together: habitat is a fixed effect, the sources were measured
separately in each habitat (`source_factors = "Habitat"`), and the sources'
elemental concentrations differ (concentration dependence). MixSIAR's script also uses
an informative "specialist" prior, which MixSIARPFN supports too. Only the fitting call
differs from MixSIAR's script: `run_pfn()` in place of `write_JAGS_model()` and
`run_model()`.

## The data

```{r load, eval = TRUE}
mix <- load_mix_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "mantis_consumer.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"), factors = "Habitat", fac_random = FALSE,
  fac_nested = FALSE, cont_effects = NULL)
source <- load_source_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "mantis_source.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  source_factors = "Habitat", conc_dep = TRUE, data_type = "means", mix)
discr <- load_discr_data(
  filename = system.file("extdata", "mantis_discrimination.csv", package = "MixSIARPFN"),
  mix)
```

There are `r mix$N` mantis shrimp in `r length(mix$FAC[[1]]$labels)` habitats
(`r paste(mix$FAC[[1]]$labels, collapse = ", ")`), and `r source$n.sources` sources
(`r paste(source$source_names, collapse = ", ")`).

```{r isospace, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 5}
plot_data(mix = mix, source = source, discr = discr)
```

## Fitting the model

Residual * Process error, and MixSIAR's specialist prior: weights 1, 1, 4, 4, 1, 4 on
the sources (in `source$source_names` order), scaled so that they sum to the number of
sources, exactly as in MixSIAR's script.

```{r prior, eval = TRUE}
alpha.spec <- c(1, 1, 4, 4, 1, 4)
alpha.spec <- alpha.spec * length(alpha.spec) / sum(alpha.spec)
setNames(round(alpha.spec, 2), source$source_names)
```

```{r fit}
time <- system.time(
  fit <- run_pfn(mix, source, discr, alpha.prior = alpha.spec,
                 resid_err = TRUE, process_err = TRUE)
)
fit
```

## Results

```{r output, results = "hide", fig.show = "hide"}
out <- output_pfn(fit, mix, source,
                  output_options = list(summary_save = FALSE, plot_post_save_pdf = FALSE))
```

```{r summary-table}
knitr::kable(round(summary_table(fit), 3))
```

```{r result-plots, fig.height = 4}
for (p in out$plots[grepl("^Habitat", names(out$plots))]) print(p)
```

MixSIAR's script goes on to combine sources after the fit (hard-shelled against
soft-bodied prey), with `combine_sources()`. That needs joint posterior draws, which
MixSIARPFN does not give, so it is not repeated here.
